subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Find the points on the line 4x−3y−10=0 which are at a distance of 5 units from the point (1,−2).

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IB (2026-27 edition), chapter 3 THE STRAIGHT LINE, Very Short Answer question 35(i), book p.146. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the volume prints a chapter-level marks banner over this section but no per-step allocation on any answer. The split gives one mark for turning the slope into cos θ and sin θ, which is what the parametric form needs, and one for reporting BOTH points; the middle step that writes the parametric point carries 0 marks because it is bookkeeping between the two marked moves. The stem is well posed: (1, −2) satisfies 4(1) − 3(−2) − 10 = 0, so the given point lies ON the line, which is what makes the parametric method available and what forces two answers rather than one. This book prints almost no exam-appearance years, so appearances[] is empty. Paper position: Maths-1B Section A runs Q1 to Q10 at 2 marks each, all compulsory, under the 2026-27 pattern. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — say what you convert the slope into, and why there are two answers.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Slope to cosθ and sinθ
steps.margin_note: First mark. Check the given point is on the line, then convert the slope: the parametric form needs cos θ and sin θ, not the slope itself.
steps.memory_tip: The parametric form needs cos θ and sin θ. From tan θ = 4/3 the 3-4-5 triangle gives both with no calculator.

recall.must_convey: That the given point is on the line and the slope 4/3 gives cos θ = 3/5 and sin θ = 4/5.
accept: the point one comma minus two is on the line
the slope is four by three so cos theta is three fifths and sin theta is four fifths
tan theta equals four over three gives the three four five triangle
slope nunchi cos theta sin theta teesukovali
convert the slope into cos and sin

steps.why: tan θ = 4/3 means the right triangle has sides 3 and 4 and hypotenuse 5, so cos θ and sin θ come out exactly. Checking that (1, −2) is on the line matters first: the parametric method measures distance ALONG the line from a point of the line.
common_mistakes: Taking cosθ = 4/5 and sinθ = 3/5, with the two swapped.
Reading the slope as −b/a and getting 3/4.

steps.label: Write the parametric point
steps.margin_note: The two points sit at distance 5 on EITHER side of (1, −2), so the ± is written into the parametric form from the start.
steps.memory_tip: The two points sit on EITHER side, so write the ± into the parametric form from the start.

recall.must_convey: That the required points are (x₁ ± r cos θ, y₁ ± r sin θ) = (1 ± 3, −2 ± 4).
accept: the points are one plus or minus three comma minus two plus or minus four
use the parametric form with plus or minus because there are two points
distance five each way along the line
rendu vaipula unnaayi kabatti plus or minus
write the parametric point with plus or minus r
heard_as: minus two plus or minus four

steps.why: A given distance from a point ON a line is reached in BOTH directions along that line, so the ± is not optional — it is what produces the two points the question asks for.
common_mistakes: Using only + and finding one point.
Multiplying 5 by cosθ and sinθ the wrong way round.

steps.label: State both required points
steps.margin_note: The last mark. Take the signs TOGETHER — both plus, then both minus. Mixing them gives points that are not on the line.
steps.memory_tip: Take the signs TOGETHER — both plus, then both minus. Mixing them gives points off the line.
lines: 4(−2) − 3(−6) − 10 = 0, so both are on the line.

recall.must_convey: That the two points are (4, 2) and (−2, −6).
accept: the points are four comma two and minus two comma minus six
take both plus signs together then both minus signs together
rendu points four two and minus two minus six

steps.why: The ± must be taken consistently in both coordinates, because they describe one step of length 5 in one direction along the line — mixing the signs steps sideways off the line. There are two answers because the given point is on the line and you can walk 5 units either way from it.
common_mistakes: Mixing the signs and reporting (4, −6) or (−2, 2).
Reporting only one of the two points.
